paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
model_annotation: The plot presents the accuracy (ACC %) of knowledge probing in a biomedical language model, BioMedLM, after being edited using different methods as a function of co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale. The x-axis represents the co-occurrence number and is plotted on a logarithmic scale due to its wide range of values, starting from 10^0 and extending to 10^3. The y-axis denotes the accuracy percentage and is marked on a linear scale. The graph features six lines, each representing a distinct editing approach: Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME, with their performances compared at predictable intervals along the logarithmic scale. The Base line is color-coded with a solid line, marking it as the lowest performing method among the six, and remains constant at around 44% accuracy across all levels of co-occurrence number. The MEND and MEMIT lines, solid and dashed respectively, exhibit moderate performance, with MEND slightly outperforming MEMIT. IKE, represented by triangles, starts similar to FT but surpasses it and shows a steep ascent in accuracy as co-occurrence frequency increases, culminating in an accuracy just above 52% at the highest co-occurrence number. The ROME line, denoted by squares, displays the most pronounced improvement, beginning near 51% and attaining the peak performance across all methods, ending roughly at 66% in perfect accuracy at the highest co-occurrence number.
